messages:
Maria C.: Heads up — us-west: we saw 3 failed scale-ups for `dedicated-gpu-pool-2` in the last 45m. A few inference pods are stuck Pending with nodeAffinity for `gpu-type=nv4` and CA didn't add nodes. Anyone else seeing this?
infra-bot: ALERT: cluster-autoscaler failed to add nodes for ASG `gpu-dedicated-west-2` (capacity reached). recent logs: `failed to scale up: ASG max size reached` :warning:
Dan T.: I can confirm ASG is at max (40). Dedicated pools were set to disallow spot fallback by policy — so when on-demand capacity exhausted CA has nowhere to go. That explains the Pending pods.
Khalid R.: Those namespaces are tier-1 latency tenants, so the policy was intentional. But we can do a controlled overflow: create a hosted-burst pool (ephemeral, preemptible) with strict taints so only flagged namespaces can tolerate it. That reduces noisy neighbor risk.
Sophie L.: Remember when we used hosted-burst before we hit NAT gateway saturation and cross-AZ ENI limits — pods got connection resets mid-inference. If we burst to an AZ without NAT headroom we break in-flight requests. We should check NAT/ENI headroom before enabling cross-AZ bursting.
Maria C.: While testing I saw one node actually join then become NotReady. Kubelet logs show an NVIDIA driver mismatch — node had driver 525 but cluster expects 530, causing `nvidia-smi` failures and the node failing GPU plugin healthcheck. Snippet:
```
Mar 22 12:14:07 kubelet[...]: Err: nvidia-smi: /lib64/libnvidia-ml.so.1: version `NVIDIA_530' not found
nvidia-device-plugin: health check failed: gpu plugin CRITICAL
```
That made CA mark the scale-up as failed because the node wasn't usable.
Ashley P.: Plan of action: 1) temporarily request ASG soft-increase +8 in us-west to relieve pressure, 2) patch node bootstrap to validate driver version and cordon if mismatch (so CA can continue), 3) introduce a namespaced feature-flag to allow spot-fallback only for batch/low-priority tenants, 4) add a pre-check in autoscaler to verify NAT/ENI headroom before launching cross-AZ nodes.
Dan T.: +1. I'll open the PR for the ASG bump and the feature-flag for namespace-level spot fallback. Also adding a Prometheus gauge `queued_pending_gpu_pods` and an alert at 3+ sustained for 5m.
Khalid R.: For the hosted-burst pool we should enforce taints: `node.kubernetes.io/hosted-burst=true:NoSchedule` and require a namespace label `burst=allowed`. That way we only route explicit overflow traffic.
Sophie L.: I'll run a quick capacity check script against us-west NAT gateways and ENI quotas and post results here. If headroom is <20% we should gate cross-AZ bursting.
Maria C.: Thanks — I'm going to pin the affected namespaces and notify CS + oncall. Creating a brief incident note with the driver mismatch and ASG bump request. /cc @infra-oncall
Dan T.: :thumbsup: will follow up with PR links and deploy plan.
Ashley P.: After we stabilize we'll run a short e2e that simulates burst on a non-prod tenant to validate NAT/ENI behaviour before enabling for prod namespaced traffic.
